tagline: Down the Clark Fork with the railroad for company.
intro: MT 135 leaves I-90 at St. Regis and follows the Clark Fork for 21 miles through the Lolo National Forest, with a rail line running alongside. The country starts out in open, rolling flats and closes into steep canyon walls. Near Quinn the river and the road straighten, and a couple of miles short of Paradise the highway comes out of the forest and meets MT 200.
On the old secondary route that ran this way from 1960 to 1978, a toll ferry took traffic across the river.

moments.title: St. Regis
moments.text: A town where the St. Regis River meets the Clark Fork, named for the river that Pierre-Jean De Smet named after a fellow Jesuit.

moments.title: The river crossing
moments.text: Near the midpoint the highway crosses the Clark Fork and ducks under the railroad, and from there road and rails keep to opposite banks.

moments.title: Paradise
moments.text: A Northern Pacific division point from 1883 near where the Flathead joins the Clark Fork, and the place where railroaders set their watches from Mountain to Pacific time.
